He was ranked as the world No. 3 in men's doubles by the [[Association of Tennis Professionals]] (ATP), winning 26 career doubles titles, including three [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]]s and an Olympic silver medal. Llodra also had success in singles, winning five career titles and with victories over [[Novak Djokovic]], [[Juan Martín del Potro]], [[Tomáš Berdych]], [[Robin Söderling]], [[Jo-Wilfried Tsonga]], [[Nikolay Davydenko]], [[Janko Tipsarević]] and [[John Isner]]. Llodra has been called "the best volleyer on tour."{{by whom|date=February 2025}} ==Life and career== [[File:2014 US Open (Tennis) - Tournament - Michael Llodra (15129919821).jpg|thumb|Llodra at 2014 US Open]] Llodra was born in [[Paris]], where his father Michel played for [[Paris Saint-Germain]]. A left-hander, his [[serve-and-volley]] style is modelled on that of his idol, [[Stefan Edberg]].{{cite web |url=http://www.tennisclubchatou.com/pages/l-organisation/ |title=Présentation du TC Chatou |website=tennisclubchatou.com |language=fr |access-date=20 October 2022 |archive-date=25 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125033534/http://www.tennisclubchatou.com/pages/l-organisation/ |url-status=dead }}. Llodra and his wife Camille were married on 9 September 2003, and have two children, a daughter, Manon (born 23 March 2004) and a son, Teo (born 5 September 2007). He is a well-known supporter of French football club Paris Saint-Germain, and has often been seen wearing the club's shirt prior to tennis matches. ===2002=== Llodra reached his first Grand Slam final, the [[2002 Australian Open – Men's doubles|Australian Open]] men's doubles, with [[Fabrice Santoro]]. Unseeded, they lost to [[Mark Knowles]] and [[Daniel Nestor]]. During his semifinal, Llodra inadvertently hit and killed a bird flying across the court.{{Cite news |date=2002-01-24 |title=Llodra gets the bird |language=en-GB |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/australian_open/1779136.stm |access-date=2023-11-04}} ===2003=== Llodra won his first Grand Slam title, the Australian Open men's doubles, with Santoro. Their opponents in the final were once again Knowles and Nestor. ===2004=== Upon winning the men's doubles again for the second time at the Australian Open in 2004, Llodra and his tennis partner Santoro made headlines by stripping off their shirts, shoes, socks and shorts.{{cite web |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/SPORT/01/31/tennis.doubles/ |title=Celebrations end with a striptease |website=CNN.com World Sport |access-date=19 May 2007 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304104020/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/SPORT/01/31/tennis.doubles/ |url-status=live }} Dressed in a pair of white briefs only, Llodra threw his clothes into the crowd, to the cheers of many onlookers.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/australian_open_2004/3446923.stm |title=French duo retain title |work=BBC News Online |date=31 January 2004 |access-date=19 May 2007 |archive-date=25 May 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060525061608/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/tennis/australian_open_2004/3446923.stm |url-status=live }} Llodra made his first appearance in the fourth round of a Grand Slam singles tournament at that year's French Open. In the fourth round he led eventual semifinalist [[Tim Henman]] by two sets to love and had a match point in the fifth set before Henman prevailed. Llodra also won his first ATP singles title two weeks later at 's-Hertogenbosch. ===2005=== On 20 November 2005, Llodra again teamed with Santoro to win the Tennis Masters Cup in Shanghai, a competition which pitted the top eight doubles teams in the world against one another. ===2007=== In July, Llodra won the [[2007 Wimbledon Championships – Men's doubles|men's doubles title at Wimbledon]] partnering [[Arnaud Clément]], defeating [[Bob and Mike Bryan]] to win his third Grand Slam doubles title. He and Clément were ecstatic, and Llodra once again celebrated by throwing his shirt, racket and towel into the crowd. At the [[2007 US Open (tennis)|US Open]], he and Clément were seeded seventh, but were upset in the second round by [[Jesse Levine]] and [[Alex Kuznetsov]]. ===2008=== Llodra and Clément reached a second Grand Slam final at the Australian Open, but lost to the Israeli pairing of [[Jonathan Erlich]] and [[Andy Ram]]. In singles, Llodra won two tournaments in the course of two months, the first in Adelaide, where he defeated [[Jarkko Nieminen]] in the final, and the other in Rotterdam, where he edged out [[Robin Söderling]] in a third-set tiebreak. Llodra and his doubles partner Clément then defeated the Bryan Brothers again in four sets at the [[Davis Cup]] quarterfinals tie against the US team. They are one of two teams to defeat the Bryans in Davis Cup. He then entered the [[2008 French Open|French Open]], where he upset [[Tomáš Berdych]] in the second round and went on to reach the fourth round, losing to Latvian [[Ernests Gulbis]] in straight sets. ===2009=== [[File:Llodra Roland Garros 2009 1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Llodra at the [[2009 French Open]].]] In 2009, he made two finals in singles; the [[2009 Open 13|Open 13]] in Marseille (l. to Tsonga) and the [[2009 Grand Prix de Tennis de Lyon|Grand Prix]] in Lyon (l. to Ljubicic). He had a poor season in doubles.{{cite web |title=Tsonga impressionne |url=http://www.eurosport.fr/tennis/atp-marseille/2009/tsonga-impressionne_sto1852054/story.shtml |website=eurosport.fr |language=fr |date=21 February 2009 |access-date=7 August 2020 |archive-date=24 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024110410/https://www.eurosport.fr/tennis/atp-marseille/2009/tsonga-impressionne_sto1852054/story.shtml |url-status=live }}. ===2010=== Llodra started off the season with opening-round losses in Brisbane and Sydney. He made the second round of the [[2010 Australian Open|Australian Open]], losing to [[Juan Mónaco]] in five sets. He lost to [[Marco Chiudinelli]] in the opening round in Rotterdam. The following week, he impressively won the [[2010 Open 13|Open 13]] tournament in Marseille. He beat two well-known players on the rise: seventh seed [[Marcos Baghdatis]] (in the second round) and top seed [[Robin Söderling]] (in the quarterfinals). In the final, he defeated [[Julien Benneteau]] in straight sets in their first meeting on the ATP tour.{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Tennis/breves2010/20100219_154418_llodra-corrige-soderling.html |title=Llodra sort Söderling |work=[[L'Équipe]] |language=fr |date=19 February 2010 |access-date=20 October 2022 |archive-date=11 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811072503/http://www.lequipe.fr/Tennis/breves2010/20100219_154418_llodra-corrige-soderling.html |url-status=dead }} Llodra and Benneteau also teamed up to win the doubles title in Marseille. Llodra also won at Eastbourne, beating [[Guillermo García-López]] in the final.{{cite web |title=Llodra, label vert |url=http://www.eurosport.fr/tennis/atp-eastbourne/2010/llodra-label-vert_sto2368074/story.shtml |website=eurosport.fr |language=fr |access-date=19 June 2010 |archive-date=22 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100622041046/http://www.eurosport.fr/tennis/atp-eastbourne/2010/llodra-label-vert_sto2368074/story.shtml |url-status=live }}. Llodra lost in the first round at the French Open, the second round at Wimbledon, and made the third round at the US Open before retiring against [[Tommy Robredo]]. At the [[BNP Paribas Masters]] tournament in Paris-Bercy, he played his best tennis in an ATP Masters 1000 tournament, where he defeated second seed [[Novak Djokovic]] and then eleventh seed [[Nikolay Davydenko]] in the quarterfinals. Llodra then held three match points against world No. 5 and eventual champion [[Robin Söderling]], but eventually lost in a third-set tiebreak. Had Llodra won, it would have been an all-French final in Paris with compatriot [[Gaël Monfils]]. ===2011=== At the Australian Open, Llodra and Zimonjic lost in the quarterfinals to [[Mahesh Bhupathi]] and [[Leander Paes]]. They reached the final in Rotterdam, but lost to [[Jürgen Melzer]] and Petzschner. They reached the semifinals in Dubai, but lost to [[Jérémy Chardy]] and [[Feliciano López]], again in a super-tiebreak. They reached the quarterfinals in Miami, again losing to Bhupathi and Paes. In Madrid, they lost the final to the Bryan brothers. In Rome, they reached the quarterfinals, losing to [[Carlos Berlocq]] and [[Jarkko Nieminen]]. The team made the semifinals at the French Open and at Wimbledon, losing to [[Max Mirnyi]] and [[Daniel Nestor]] in a match featuring two tiebreaks, and to the Bryan brothers in five sets. They won their first two titles of the year in Washington, D.C., and at the Canadian Open, against [[Robert Lindstedt]] and [[Horia Tecău]] and the Bryan brothers, respectively. They lost in the final in Cincinnati, again against Bhupathi and Paes. They did not make it past the round of 16 at the US Open, but they took their third title of the year at the China Open, again against Lindstedt and Tecau. They lost in the final in Shanghai against [[Max Mirnyi]] and Nestor in a super-tiebreak. They took their fourth title together in Basel, again defeating Mirnyi and Nestor in the final. They reached the quarterfinals in Bercy and participated in the [[2011 ATP World Tour Finals]] in London, winning their first round-robin match against [[Rohan Bopanna]] and [[Aisam Qureshi]]. In singles, Llodra reached the quarterfinals in Marseille, losing to [[Robin Söderling]]. He also reached the quarterfinals in Madrid, losing to finalist [[Rafael Nadal]]. He lost in the first round at the French Open and in the round of 16 at Wimbledon. In the US Open, he lost in the second round to [[Kevin Anderson (tennis)|Kevin Anderson]] in straight sets. ===2012=== At the [[2012 BNP Paribas Masters – Singles|BNP Paribas Masters]] in Paris (Bercy), Llodra reached the semifinals, after upsetting tenth and seventh seeds [[John Isner]] and [[Juan Martín del Potro]], even though he was the lowest-ranked player in the draw. He also beat American [[Sam Querrey]] in the quarterfinals. He faced [[David Ferrer]] for a place in the final, but lost.{{Cite web |title=L'Équipe - L'actualité du sport en continu. |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Tennis/Actualites/Llodra-double-peine/269617 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr |access-date=21 October 2022 |archive-date=9 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120709070813/http://www.lequipe.fr/Tennis/Actualites/Llodra-double-peine/269617 |url-status=live }} ===2013=== At the [[2013 Dubai Tennis Championships|Dubai Open]], Llodra stunned world No. 8 and [[2008 Australian Open – Men's singles|Australian Open 2008]] finalist [[Jo-Wilfried Tsonga]] in straight sets, but lost to [[Dmitry Tursunov]] in the next round. Llodra was also in the men's doubles finals of the French Open with [[Nicolas Mahut]], but lost to the Bryan brothers in the final.{{Cite web |title=Llodra impuissant face à Murray |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/sports/tennis/us-open/actualites/llodra-impuissant-face-a-murray-649605 |website=LEFIGARO |language=fr |date=29 August 2013 |access-date=21 October 2022 |archive-date=21 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021051954/https://www.lefigaro.fr/sports/tennis/us-open/actualites/llodra-impuissant-face-a-murray-649605 |url-status=live }} ===2014=== In 2014 Llodra played fewer tournaments and had less success in singles than the previous years. He suffered first-round losses at the [[2014 Australian Open|Australian Open]] and [[2014 French Open|French Open]], and skipped [[2014 Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]]. He did, however, get a win at the [[2014 US Open (tennis)|US Open]], defeating [[Daniel Gimeno-Traver]]. ==Playing style== Llodra was known for his skilled net play.{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/04/sports/tennis/04llodra.html |title=Llodra's Strong Net Play to Match His Sense of Humor |work=The New York Times |date=4 September 2010 |access-date=20 November 2010 |archive-date=12 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130812031729/http://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/04/sports/tennis/04llodra.html |url-status=live |last1=Clarey |first1=Christopher }} ''[[The Guardian]]'' journalist Xan Brooks described Llodra as "one of those talented, maddening French players in the tradition of [[Henri Leconte]], [[Guy Forget]] and [[Fabrice Santoro]]; at once supremely gifted and curiously brittle" and that he "plays like he's just flown in from the 20th-century. His game is all dinks and slices and sly changes of pace."{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/jun/23/wimbledon-2010-tennis-live |title=Wimbledon 2010 live blog |work=The Guardian |date=23 June 2010 |access-date=6 October 2010 |archive-date=22 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131222161722/http://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/jun/23/wimbledon-2010-tennis-live |url-status=live |last1=Brooks |first1=Xan }} Two-time French Open finalist [[Robin Söderling]] called Llodra's serve "unbelievable" and his volleys the "best on the tour".{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/nov/13/robin-soderling-michael-llodra |title=Robin Soderling halts Michael Llodra's run in Paris Masters |work=The Guardian |date=13 November 2010 |access-date=20 November 2010 |archive-date=13 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313230419/http://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/nov/13/robin-soderling-michael-llodra |url-status=live }} To aid his touch on volleys, Llodra was one of the few professionals to use all natural gut strings, which gave him better feel at the expense of power at the baseline. Llodra was one of the last remaining [[serve-and-volley]]ers in the top ranks of men's professional tennis, a tactic aided by his left-handed serve which allowed him to create unusual angles. Llodra has been called the 'best serve and volleyer in the world' by the website Essential Tennis.{{cite web |url=http://essentialtennis.com/tournews/2010/07/best-serve-and-volleyer-in-the-world/ |title=Best Serve and Volleyer in the World |work=Essential Tennis |access-date=6 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110523065818/http://essentialtennis.com/tournews/2010/07/best-serve-and-volleyer-in-the-world/ |archive-date=23 May 2011}} ==Significant finals== ===Grand Slam finals=== ====Doubles: 7 (3 titles, 4 runner-ups)==== {|class="sortable wikitable" !Result !Year !style="width:130px"|Championship !Surface !style="width:135px"|Partner !style="width:135px"|Opponents !style="width:150px" class="unsortable"|Score |- | style="background:#ffa07a;"|Loss | [[2002 Australian Open – Men's doubles|2002]] | style="background:#ffffcc;"|[[Australian Open]] | Hard | {{flagicon|FRA}} [[Fabrice Santoro]] | {{flagicon|BAH}} [[Mark Knowles]]

Open]] men's doubles semifinal against [[Julien Boutter]] and [[Arnaud Clément]], a small bird (identified as a [[house martin]]) flew into the court chasing a [[moth]]. It flew into the path of a hard-hit volley by Llodra. After an impromptu funeral ceremony led by Boutter, the match continued, with Llodra and Santoro eventually winning 6–3, 3–6, 12–10.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/australian_open/1779136.stm |title=Llodra gets the bird |work=BBC News |date=24 January 2002 |access-date=29 January 2010 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304142510/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/australian_open/1779136.stm |url-status=live }} Llodra remarked afterwards, "I didn't do it deliberately. But at least I saved the moth." ===Nude in the locker=== In the 2005 [[Miami Open (tennis)|Key Biscayne tournament]], Llodra was hiding nude in [[Ivan Ljubicic]]'s locker. When Ljubicic discovered him, Llodra stated that he "tried to get his positive energy".{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/news/story?id=2023416 |title=Prankster Llodra nude in Croatian's locker |work=ESPN |date=28 March 2005 |access-date=27 May 2016 |archive-date=4 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604223123/http://espn.go.com/sports/tennis/news/story?id=2023416 |url-status=live }} In 2005 Ljubicic was playing his most successful season by then. ===Accusation of racism=== After his first round victory over [[Ernests Gulbis]] at the 2012 BNP Paribas Open at Indian Wells, during which Llodra was overheard by fans and journalists making racist and sexist comments to a female Gulbis fan, Llodra was fined $2500 by the ATP for his behaviour.{{cite web |url=http://www.tennis.com/articles/templates/thespin.aspx?articleid=16823&zoneid=32 |title=After racial taunt, Michael Llodra pays a price beyond money |website=tennis.com}} He later admitted making the comments in interviews with French media and complained that the fine was too high. Llodra did not make matters better for himself during an interview with a reporter from the Chinese news Web site SINA.com, in which the Frenchman attempted to apologize for his remarks. "My words were not aimed at China," Llodra began. "I love Chinese — I can totally make love with a Chinese girl," he added, before being cut off by the A.T.P. official monitoring the interview. The journalist, who took offense at the remark, said that he did not find Llodra's apology sincere. This was not the first incident in which charges of racism have been leveled at Llodra.{{cite web |title=Michael Llodra racism incident
